source.title: SPRKD: Effective Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks via Saddle Region Approximation
source.authors: Aditya Dewan; Arjun Yogeswaran; B. Fedoruk

record.tranche_reason: The study measures Hessian curvature and validation performance in trained students, bearing conceptually on whether a trained network property tracks generalization. It does not test the specific versions as stated.
record.gate_note: The study does not test random-label memorization, interpolation-width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. It reports Hessian and validation results; cited findings from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a distillation method, validation accuracy, and Hessian curvature. None tests V1–V8. Its curvature results are related to V7, but it does not measure magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, train–test gaps, similarly low training losses, or rankings against norm- and margin-based measures. Citing sharp-minima work does not test its batch-size claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that weak-teacher SPRKD surpasses response KD, matches scratch-trained malaria controls in accuracy, and reaches smoother, wider minima with lower Hessian curvature. They interpret this geometry as indicating stronger generalization and stability. The record should qualify its claim of higher validation performance: the authors report statistical equivalence to Control-S on malaria, while supplementary benchmarks show preliminary numerical advantages. Generalization gaps and magnitude-aware sharpness are not measured.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses weak-teacher saddle-region distillation, Hessian-based measurements, and validation performance; it does not use the interventions or measurements specified by the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports differences by model and dataset; the supplementary benchmark results are preliminary qualitative findings.

fits_no_version.finding: On malaria, SPRKD has validation accuracy 94.80% and Hessian trace 33.39, versus 94.47% and 71.33 for Control-S, and 70.10% and 408.27 for RKD. The authors report no significant accuracy difference from Control-S.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this distillation comparison, lower raw Hessian trace accompanies higher numerical validation accuracy, with a statistically significant accuracy advantage reported only against response KD.

fits_no_version.finding: Preliminary epoch-10 results report SPRKD versus scratch-control validation accuracy of 96% versus 88% on CIFAR-100 and 99% versus 97% on MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SPRKD improves reported early validation accuracy over scratch training in these supplementary experiments.

record.problems: The authors state that TinyImageNet results are qualitative only and that supplementary benchmark results have no dedicated results table. The main malaria comparison averages 5 trials, but the reported table gives no uncertainty intervals. The study does not report a train–test gap or test magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. TinyImageNet is described only as qualitative findings without a separately attributable numerical result.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architectures and training recipes.
Test-error behavior when widening beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparisons and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization gaps among similarly low-training-loss networks, and comparative ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: All ten rows describe the study's method evaluation or its comparators and belong under fits_no_version. None warrants a verdict on V1–V8. No additional result bearing on those versions is missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance under the same recipes.
Width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning conditions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptive recipes.
Dropout comparisons and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations and their association with train–test gaps among similarly low-training-loss networks.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting held-out accuracy.

rows.subject: SPRKD
rows.operation_detail: Measured validation accuracy on malaria blood-smear classification.
rows.check: 94.80% is correctly transcribed, but this is the proposed method's performance, not an observation of a listed claim. The malaria advantage over Control-S is 0.33 percentage points; the authors report McNemar p = 1.0.

rows.subject: Control-Student (Control-S)
rows.operation_detail: Measured validation accuracy on malaria blood-smear classification.
rows.note: Scratch-trained student with the same architecture as SPRKD; reported as averaged across 5 trials.
rows.check: Correctly transcribed method-comparison baseline; validation accuracy alone measures no listed version.

rows.subject: RKD
rows.operation_detail: Measured task validation accuracy after response knowledge distillation.
rows.check: Correctly transcribed response-distillation comparator; it does not test a listed version.
